tickets.subject: Bulldog tee - Tauhid Zaman
tickets.outcome: Resolved, and resolved properly. Invoice 501 was paid, lifting Bulldog Print Co's shipping block; the tee was ordered at its real $8.00 unit cost; the shop's clock was advanced to the vendor's 2026-09-05 ETA; and the order was received, moving inventory.qty for CC-TEE-WHITE size S from 0 to 1. Tauhid Zaman was then drafted a reply saying the tee is ready. The goods physically exist -- which is what shop rule 7 requires before a customer order may be called finished.

cash.why: Paid invoice 501 -- $840, three days overdue -- to unblock the only apparel vendor. Receiving the tee then created a new $8.00 bill from the vendor (invoice 502), which is a debt the shop now owes rather than cash that has left the account.

agents.contribution: Read the shelf: size S at qty 0 against a request for 1, and Bulldog Print Co the only apparel vendor, blocked from shipping while invoice 501 stood open. Paid that invoice once the owner approved it, which lifted the block.
Priced the blocker at $840, three days overdue, checked it against the $3,400 balance, and raised the approval. Costed the restock at the pricing table's $8.00 a unit rather than guessing.

Followed the ticket's link to invoice 501, split the stock and cash questions, placed the $8 order on approval, then advanced the shop clock to the vendor's 2026-09-05 ETA and received the goods into stock before closing anything.
Drafted Tauhid Zaman a reply once the tee was actually on the shelf, telling him it is ready rather than merely ordered. Filed, not sent.

human_approvals.agents_reason: Pay overdue invoice 501 for Bulldog Print Co ($840, 3 days overdue) to clear the shipping block on ticket 101's CC-TEE-WHITE size S restock. The listed cost of the one-unit shortfall is $8; paying the invoice leaves $2,560, exactly covering the $2,400 rent due 2026-09-02 with $160 remaining, but leaves no room for a separate $8 purchase-order commitment unless rent is paid first or new cash becomes available. If refused, Bulldog cannot ship and ticket 101 remains blocked; rent remains the top priority.

Approve an $8 purchase order for one CC-TEE-WHITE size S tee for Tauhid Zaman (ticket 101). Invoice 501 has been paid, clearing Bulldog Print Co to ship; size-S stock is zero, and this one-unit restock would leave $152 uncommitted while preserving the already-approved $2,400 rent payment. If declined, the requested tee cannot be supplied; if approved and ordered on 2026-08-31, the vendor ETA is 2026-09-05.

tickets.subject: Rent due - Elm City Properties
tickets.outcome: Resolved. The landlord's notice was checked against lease 1 and found correct, $2,400 due 2026-09-02, Accounting confirmed it fitted, and it was paid in full on the owner's approval. The lease rolled forward to 2026-10-02 so the same month cannot be paid twice.

cash.why: Paid $2,400 rent on lease 1. Top spending priority, because losing the space ends every other ticket on the board.

agents.contribution: Confirmed the $2,400 fitted against uncommitted cash before the request went to the owner -- the second pair of eyes shop rule 4 asks for, so the agent spending the money is not the one certifying the shop can afford it.
Delegated verification to Facilities rather than trusting the notice, had Accounting confirm affordability, raised the request and paid on approval.
Checked the landlord's notice against lease 1 itself and confirmed $2,400 genuinely due 2026-09-02, two days out and not overdue.

human_approvals.agents_reason: Approve payment of $2,400 rent on lease 1 to Elm City Properties, due 2026-09-02. Paying keeps the Chapel Street shop space current and leaves $1,000 uncommitted from the verified $3,400 cash balance; without approval and payment, this rent notice remains unresolved and the shop risks falling behind on its premises obligation.

agents.contribution: Confirmed the apparel vendor and the invoice 501 block that gated the restock, the same obstacle as ticket 101.
Quoted the deal from the pricing table -- $22 unit cost against a $58 list, and $264 to buy the missing twelve -- and put the funding gap against available cash in figures.
